key_insight: Biot–Savart-inspired activations improve incompressible-flow PINNs, with fixed- and learnable-scale variants reducing combined velocity error by 31.7% and 33.2% on average versus tanh-based PINNs.
engineering_relevance: Embedding analytical flow structure in network activations could improve neural incompressible-flow simulations, including localized shear and vortex dynamics.
method: Extract a smooth rational activation from a regularized Biot–Savart kernel.
Use either fixed or learnable kernel scales.
Retain the standard velocity–pressure formulation and physics-informed training.
evidence_signal: Across 21 benchmark–architecture comparisons spanning five flows, both variants consistently reduced combined velocity error; reported pressure and vorticity errors also improved.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational overhead or generalization beyond the tested benchmarks and architectures.
paper_title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
